drafted_from: tool row in tools/benchmark-small-local-models/tool-rows.json, do-work/rank_candidate_frames.py and test/test_benchmark.py (Ranks)
start_here: Say to your AI: "Rank the three candidate clips for slot 1, a person at a blue screen, with the siglip model some/clip, and tell me if its best is the one my editor would pick."

lists.label: Settings
lists.holds: One row per tool and scope (a person, a film, a piece or the whole account): the settings that tool reads when it runs, as JSON.

instructions: 1. Pour the two example settings rows into your own list:settings (see pour), or write your own row record:setting:benchmark-small-local-models~person~<you> whose settings hold {"commands":{"rank_candidate_frames":{...your defaults}}}.
2. Say the line in start_here. Your AI reads this tool's row with tools:list {tool: "tool:rank-candidate-clips-for-a-slot-with-small-local-models"} and gets its run command.

3. Your AI writes the request as a JSON file (request.json), adds settings_record from your settings row if you keep one, and runs python3 trillion-workshop/tools/benchmark-small-local-models/do-work/rank_candidate_frames.py request.json on your computer.
4. It reads the last line the script prints: {"result": ...} or {"error": "what to change"} (exit code 2), then tells you the result in plain words.
5. method is one of siglip, decider-vision, decider-text, bge-text or qwen3vl; any other word is refused with the list of five.

worked_examples.title: Three candidates ranked; the model's best matches the editor's
worked_examples.ask: Which candidate clip fits slot 1 best?
worked_examples.given: From tools/benchmark-small-local-models/test/test_benchmark.py (Ranks.test_every_method_ranks_and_agreement_counts_the_reference), method siglip, with the test's stand-in model. request.json = {"slots":[{"slot":1,"desc":"a person at a blue screen","cands":[{"frame":"c0.png","text":"red lamp"},{"frame":"c1.png","text":"blue screen person"},{"frame":"c2.png","text":"wide"}]}],"method":"siglip","model":"some/clip","device":"cpu","reference":{"1":["c1","c0","c2"]},"reference_name":"editor"}. Run: python3 trillion-workshop/tools/benchmark-small-local-models/do-work/rank_candidate_frames.py request.json
worked_examples.hands_back: {"result":{"meta":{"method":"siglip","model":"some/clip","n":3,...},"scores":{"c0.png":0.023,"c1.png":1.0,"c2.png":0.023},"rank":{"1":["c1.png","c2.png","c0.png"]},"agreement":{"top1":"1/1","top1_in_editor_top3":"1/1"}}}: c1.png (blue screen person) is ranked first, the same as the editor's first, so top1 is 1/1. With "method":"nope" it answers {"error":"method 'nope' is not siglip, decider-vision, decider-text, bge-text or qwen3vl"}.

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for the same job and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and this kit list as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
